All four are recorded as gaps on main ([228](https://github.com/AaronAbuUsama/architect/pull/228)).

e44.text:
**One action serves everything**
The page, MCP and the CLI call the same action. It knows who is calling (a person, or an agent for that person), returns a declared refusal without writing anything, and asks for approval once.

e52.html:
// src/web/document.ts   (yours: your own component, on UI SDK)
import { definePrimitive, createChange } from "@ui-sdk/core";

export const document = definePrimitive({
  name: "document",
  options: { blocks: "value", onBlocksChange: "callback" },
  controlled: ["blocks"],          // the agent can read every block
  state: (o) => ({ blocks: o.blocks ?? [] }),
  api: (context) => {
    const change = createChange(context);
    return {
      setText: (id, text) => change("blocks", withText(id, text)),
      insert: (after, kind) => change("blocks", withBlock(after, kind)),
      move: (id, to) => change("blocks", moved(id, to)),
    };
  },
  agent: { actions: ["setText", "insert", "move"] },
});
// Saving goes through a generated action: savePage.run(...)

e53.text:
**When to write one**
Like the editor. Declaring `blocks` as controlled lets an agent read the whole page; `agent.actions` limits what it may do. Anything saved goes through a generated action, which checks the role.

e58.text:
**Catches they found**
- A refusal reaches an agent only through UI SDK's `pending` and `error` keys, read from its code, not its docs.
- Who pressed (person or agent) reaches only callbacks, so the send goes through `dispatch` and `settle`: one shared function.
- A React-controlled text box swallows UI SDK's "/" menu. Let UI SDK own the value.
- An agent can't read text outside a component's declared state.

e62.text:
**Verdict: derive, don't declare**
No components or screens in the blueprint. Generate typed pieces from operations, reads and moves; add only the missing meaning. Reopen only if a component ever carries meaning no operation has.

import { Handle } from "../thing.ts";

e60.text:
**The case for it**
- The types reach the page.
- The page's agent gets exactly the blueprint's actions.
- Journeys run through the real page; the portal lists every screen.
- An agent writes a small declaration the compiler checks.

e37.text: Actions are the spine; screens use generated, typed pieces.

e61.text:
**The case against it**
- Every win comes from generating pieces out of what the blueprint already says.
- The agent's real limit is the action: anything that saves goes through one, and it checks the role.
- Screens change daily, meaning slowly; this ties UI churn to the proven core.
- It repeats UI SDK, whose components already declare state and agent steps.
- It's the scope creep you wanted to avoid.

e41.text:
**Add the missing meaning**
- what kind a value is: a handle, a web address, a choice
- approval on an operation

Secret and private fields already exist; only their mapping onto the page's agent marks is missing. Every output uses these, not just screens.

e57.text:
**Second spike: a real world** ([222](https://github.com/AaronAbuUsama/architect/pull/222))
The same form claimed a real name through Plugged In's real code, in Chromium, for a person and for an agent, and replayed a real journey. Secret, hidden and person-only marks map cleanly; approval can't be declared yet. 16 tests.

**Pages are yours**
Arrange the generated pieces however you like. Rename a field in the blueprint and this stops compiling. Nothing about pages goes in the blueprint.

// generated/handle-claim.react.tsx   (generated, on UI SDK)
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldLabel } from "@ui-sdk/react/field";
import { Input } from "@ui-sdk/react/input";

export const HandleClaimForm = ({ action, onDone }) => {
  const [name, setName] = useState("");
  return (
    <parts.Root aria-label="Claim handle" name={name} onDone={onDone}
      onSend={(payload, details) => details.settle(action.run(payload, {
        caller: callerOf(details.source), approved: true }))}>
      <Field name="name">
        <FieldLabel>Name</FieldLabel>
        <Input value={name} onValueChange={setName} />
        <FieldDescription>Up to 32 lowercase letters and digits.</FieldDescription>
      </Field>
      <parts.Refusal>{(s) => `Refused: ${s.name} (${s.code})`}</parts.Refusal>
      <parts.Submit>Claim</parts.Submit>
    </parts.Root>
  );
};

e47.text:
**What the agent sees**
The agent bridge lists exactly the action's steps. A refusal fails the agent's step with its code. Inputs, labels and help text come from the blueprint's values.
